findings.finding: Covenant arithmetic from the company's own documents: the amended credit agreement allows max net leverage 4.50x at 2026-09-30 and 4.00x from 2026-12-31. Net leverage was 4.0x at Q2 on trailing adj EBITDA of about $72.6m (Q3'25 $29m + Q4'25 $40m + Q1'26 -$8.3m + Q2'26 $11.9m) against about $292m net debt. Dec-31 trailing EBITDA = Q1 -8.3 + Q2 11.9 + Q3 + Q4. The low end of the FY guide ($78m) gives about 3.8-3.9x at ~$290-300m net debt, so a FY EBITDA guide cut of a few million or more at this print would put the Dec-31 test at or over 4.00x and imply another amendment. The guide line therefore carries covenant consequences on top of the usual guide-cut reaction, on a company that cut FY EBITDA from $105-120m (Feb) to $78-88m (Jul).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print with a weak FY2026 guide: -27.9%. Jul 2026 print with the FY guide cut to $810-840m / $78-88m but bookings at a record: +6.8%. Apr 2026: -8.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant steps and the 4.0x figure are public, but no note found ties the Dec-31 4.00x test to the size of a possible FY guide cut. Rosenblatt's downgrade speaks only of ~$290m net debt at high rates. If this were priced, the stock would already trade as though an amendment were certain. The equity, at about 0.8x net debt, is partly there already, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Net leverage 4.0x and $45m cash at Q2 come from the call highlights (https://www.tradingview.com/news/marketbeat:a36b588ce094b:0-ribbon-communications-q2-earnings-call-highlights/). Q3'25 EBITDA of $29m is from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1708055/000110465925101530/tm2529231d1_ex99-1.htm. Q4'25 EBITDA of $40m and the original FY26 guide of $105-120m are from https://www.telecomtv.com/content/access-evolution/ribbon-communications-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial-results-54792/. These are all the company's own numbers, so they are not independent of each other. Caveat: the credit-agreement EBITDA definition may differ from adj EBITDA, but the company's reported 4.0x matches this calculation.

findings.finding: Verizon reported on 2026-10-26, after Ribbon last spoke. Its Q3 2026 capex was $3,716m against $4,310m in Q3 2025 (-14% YoY), and 9-month capex was $11.93bn against $12.26bn. Verizon is a >10% Ribbon customer, and its delayed voice-network modernization drove Cloud & Edge's -19% YoY in Q2. The FY capex guide of $16.0-16.5bn is unchanged, which implies Q4 capex of $4.1-4.6bn, up from Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Cloud & Edge -19% YoY on lower Verizon sales, and the stock still rose +6.8% because the quarter beat the guide midpoint. Feb 2026: Q4 revenue miss blamed on customer/project delays, -27.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It landed the day before the print, and RBBN previews quote only the company guide and consensus. It is a proxy, because total capex is not voice-switch spend, and the unchanged FY guide pushes spend into Q4. That is why it is filed small.
findings.independence: Rosenblatt's 2026-09-14 downgrade cites the delayed Verizon voice-modernization program and says other carriers are waiting on Verizon (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/rosenblatt-downgrades-ribbon-communications-stock-rating-on-lack-of-catalysts-93CH-4900604). Q2 call: voice switch upgrades slower than expected (TradingView highlights, above).

findings.finding: Rosenblatt downgraded RBBN Buy to Neutral on 2026-09-14 and cut the target from $3.50 to $2.20 (14x a 2027 EPS estimate cut earlier from $0.22 to $0.17). It cited no visibility on sustainable catalysts, two years of slipping telecom and federal projects, ~$290m net debt at high rates, and limited DCI exposure on Cisco-sourced technology. Five analysts cut estimates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print reaction on an analyst view. The stock went from about $2.00 at the downgrade to $1.32 on 2026-10-16.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the stock fell about 30% after it. It is filed because it is the only sourced sell-side read on why Q3/Q4 Tier-1 timing could slip again, and sized near zero for that reason.
findings.independence: Same Verizon-delay thesis as finding 2. The two share a theme but not a document, and this one is sized to its marginal content only.

findings.finding: IP Optical demand is corroborated after Ribbon last spoke. Ribbon's own Q2 IP Optical book-to-bill was 1.6x, with record bookings, backlog up more than 60% YTD and defense revenue +60% q/q. Nokia's Q3 2026 Optical Networks grew +18% cc YoY (2026-10-22), and Ciena's FQ3 2026 revenue rose +37% with the FY guide raised (2026-09-03). That supports the ~40% of revenue in IP Optical ($82m in Q2) reaching the sequential step-up inside the Q3 guide. Net of the rest: Cloud & Edge ($111m, Verizon-dependent) still has to grow for the total to reach $222.5m, so the peer read covers less than half the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: IP Optical +30% q/q with record bookings, and the stock rose +6.8% despite a FY guide cut. That is the one recent print where optical strength was rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: RBBN fell about 24% in the 20 sessions spanning both peer prints, so the market is not reading Nokia's or Ciena's optical strength through to RBBN. Rosenblatt argues RBBN's DCI exposure is small, which is why this is sized as a proxy and net of Cloud & Edge.
findings.independence: Ciena FQ3 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000936395/000162828026060245/ex9912026q3earningspressre.htm), a different company and date. RBBN's own Q2 IP Optical bookings and backlog (https://www.tradingview.com/news/marketbeat:a36b588ce094b:0-ribbon-communications-q2-earnings-call-highlights/) are a company-level document. Peer growth is AI/cloud-led, while RBBN's optical is mostly service provider and defense.
